metadata.note: The Utica and Black River Railroad (U&BR), added at the user's request from https://oneida.nygenweb.net/towns/utica/railroad.html, was Utica's own line north into the Black River valley and, eventually, the North Country -- a corridor distinct from the already-mapped NYC Adirondack Division (see nyc_adirondack_division.geojson), which took a different route via Remsen through the middle of the Adirondacks. Incorporated 1853, the U&BR reached Boonville within two years (by 1855), Lowville by 1868, and Carthage by 1872 -- 35 miles to Boonville alone. From Carthage it reached Watertown and Sackets Harbor by leasing the separate Carthage, Watertown and Sackets Harbor Railroad (1871-1875), shown here as a second feature. The U&BR itself was leased to the Rome, Watertown and Ogdensburg Railroad in 1886 (see watertown_rome_railroad.geojson) and consolidated into the New York Central and Hudson River Railroad in 1913. Sources also describe further real extensions from Carthage toward Clayton/Ogdensburg and, much later, a connection to Malone (cut at Lyons Falls in the 1960s) -- but no source found gave a confidently datable company or opening year for the Carthage-Clayton-Ogdensburg segment specifically (a rival, the Ogdensburg, Clayton and Rome Railroad, was chartered 1853 to build exactly this route but was never completed), so that segment is not traced here rather than guessed at. Geometry for the U&BR main line and the Watertown-Sackets Harbor stretch of the CW&SH is real-traced from OpenStreetMap; the Carthage-Watertown stretch (~24km) is a straight-line approximation -- the real track connecting those two points only resolved via an absurd ~310km loop down through the whole regional rail network, so a straight line was used instead. COLOR SPLIT 2026-08-24: per the same-company-same-color rule, feature(s) whose ownership passed to the New York Central were split at the documented transfer date into a pre-NYC feature (original company color) and an NYC-colored feature (matching new_york_central.geojson's canonical color), sharing identical geometry, rather than coloring the whole multi-era line with the original company's color throughout.
sources: https://oneida.nygenweb.net/towns/utica/railroad.html (Utica and Black River Railroad: incorporated Jan 31 1853; groundbreaking Aug 27 1853 with Governor Horatio Seymour; completed Utica-Boonville within two years; 1857 timetable detail -- single daily train, fares, locomotive names; two daily round trips from 1858 due to Trenton Falls resort traffic; foreclosure Nov 2 1860; reorganized May 22 1861; leased to RW&O April 14 1886; consolidated into NYC&HR April 16 1913; shared Utica station with NYC; zero passenger fatalities in 31 years of U&BR operation)

search results citing: U&BR reached Lowville 1868, Carthage 1872 (four years after Lowville); from Carthage the line reached Clayton then Ogdensburg in one direction and Sacketts Harbor/Watertown in the other (via the leased Carthage, Watertown & Sacketts Harbor); U&BR merged into RW&O 1886; the RW&O/U&BR route reached Malone as recently as 1961, cut at Lyons Falls in the 1960s

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carthage,_Watertown_and_Sackets_Harbor_Railroad (incorporated 1871, opened 1875; Sackets Harbor to Watertown, joining the RW&O; built partly on the former Sackets Harbor and Ellisburg Railroad's bed within Sackets Harbor village; incorporated into New York Central 1893; ceased operating 1949)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ogdensburg,_Clayton_and_Rome_Railroad (rival line chartered April 7 1853 to build Carthage-Clayton-Ogdensburg competing with the Black River and Utica; never completed; lost its charter 1859)
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap (via Overpass API, overpass.openstreetmap.fr mirror): railway=rail (active) combined with railway=abandoned/disused tagging, Utica to Carthage; routed via Dijkstra shortest path between geocoded station coordinates.

Carthage - Watertown - Sackets Harbor was re-traced 2026-08-24 from the OSM route relations rather than by routing between geocoded points. The earlier Dijkstra attempt had failed on this branch (310 km routed against 24 km straight line) and had been replaced with a straight-line fallback for Carthage-Watertown; that fallback, and an out-and-back excursion at the Watertown end that ran 6 km up a different line and back, are both gone. Relation members: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/1376473 and https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/1376470 (pulled via https://www.openstreetmap.org/api/0.6/relation/<id>/full.json). The Commons Data:New York Central Railroad.map behind the Wikipedia system map was checked as a cross-source and does NOT cover this branch - its nearest geometry stops at Carthage, 22 km short of Watertown.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Exact frequency/timetable for any era beyond the sourced 1857-1858 detail; the company and opening date for the real Carthage-Clayton-Ogdensburg segment (not traced here); precise date/company for the eventual Malone connection. Also unsourced: the documented route mileage of the Carthage, Watertown and Sackets Harbor. The traced length is 30.2 miles (about 18.9 Carthage-Watertown and 11.3 Watertown-Sackets Harbor), but no source found states the company's own mileage; a figure of '18 miles, Sackets Harbor to Pierrepont Manor' turns up in search results but describes the separate Sackets Harbor and Ellisburg Railroad, so it is recorded here rather than adopted.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

segments.note: Incorporated January 31 1853; groundbreaking August 27 1853 with Governor Horatio Seymour presiding. Completed Utica-Boonville (35 miles) within two years, crossing the 'hard rolling country of the upper Canada creek' near Trenton Falls on a notable high trestle. Opened with a single daily passenger train each way (Boonville 8am-Utica 10:20am, return 4pm-6:20pm); fares 75 cents to Trenton, $1.25 to Boonville; four locomotives (T.S. Faxton, J. Butterfield, D.C. Jenney, Boonville). Expanded to two daily round trips in 1858 due to the popularity of the Trenton Falls resort. Foreclosed November 2 1860, reorganized as the Utica & Black River Railroad Company May 22 1861.

Frequency estimated, unsourced.

properties.geometry_quality: Re-traced 2026-08-24 from OpenStreetMap route relations 1376473 ("Carthage Branch", old_railway_operator=NYC) and 1376470 ("Sackets Harbor Branch", old_railway_operator=NYC), both sourced in OSM to the 1917 Moody's Manual. Member ways were chained by shared nodes, the relation's Carthage-Newton Falls leg (its alt_name "Newton Falls Branch", already drawn separately in nyc_north_country_branches.geojson) was dropped, and the remaining chains were joined Carthage - Watertown - Sackets Harbor. 511 points, 48.6 km / 30.2 mi. 29 of the 30 OSM ways used carry old_railway_operator=NYC; the one exception is a short highway=residential way ("Black River Parkway") in Watertown where the right of way is now a street. Approximations, all short: five bridged gaps between chains at 0.62, 0.28, 0.07, 0.06, 0.03 km, and a 371 m straight connector at the start joining the Carthage end to the Utica & Black River feature's own Carthage endpoint so the two lines touch at the junction. This REPLACES the previous geometry, in which Carthage-Watertown was a 24 km straight-line fallback and the Watertown end carried a 6 km out-and-back excursion onto another line.

segments.note: The Carthage, Watertown and Sackets Harbor Railroad, incorporated 1871, opened in 1875, running from Sackets Harbor eastward to join the Rome, Watertown and Ogdensburg Railroad at Watertown (built within the village of Sackets Harbor partly on the railbed of the former Sackets Harbor and Ellisburg Railroad). Leased by the Utica and Black River Railroad, extending that company's reach from Carthage to Watertown and Sackets Harbor. Frequency estimated, unsourced.
